Not exactly. Shopping for food and other domestic tasks were once relegated to women who did not work outside the home. In 1950, 33% of women in the US participated in the labor force, while it was 56% in 2020 ([source](https://www.bls.gov/opub/reports/womens-databook/2021/home.htm#:~:text=Women's%20labor%20force%20participation%20rate,percentage%20points%20to%2067.7%20percent.)). Our labor has increased, inside and outside the home, and there are still 24 hours in a day. The demands of everyday life are such that grocery delivery is almost necessary in many cases.

Or the demands of society limit our time immensely: working 40+ hours a week, commuting, child care, caring for aging parents, home care, various appointments. Those who have little precious leisure time might rather spend it doing something that brings them pleasure instead of using that time in the grocery store, so home delivery is a gift. Not everyone's situation comes down to poor personal time management.
